Key.English: Cannot reload: the magazines are in the %1. Take one out first.
Cannot throw: the grenades are in the %1. Take one out first.

Sets the cells of uniforms, vests,
backpacks, crates and vehicles, as
class:size pairs separated by commas.

A number is that many cells, laid out
like the container's own pockets or
pouches. WxH is one compartment W cells
wide and H high - join several with +.

Example:
V_PlateCarrier1_rgr:20,
B_AssaultPack_rgr:30,
B_Carryall_cbr:6x4+2x3+2x3

Use the uniform's or vest's own class.
A class counts for every class based on
it, unless that one is listed itself.

Wins over the rules text, config and
the load per cell. A number goes up to
320 cells, compartments up to 8 wide
and 40 high, 24 of them and 320 cells
in all. The rules text does the same:
class=B_Carryall_Base+ > grid=6x4+2x3

A mission can give one crate, vehicle
or unit's uniform, vest or backpack
container its own grid, which wins
over all of this: the object variable
einv_grid, e.g. "6x4+2x3".

Entries that cannot be read are left
out and named in the RPT.

What a script, a loadout or the engine's
own commands (addItem, addMagazine, ACE)
put into a uniform, vest or backpack
beyond its cells moves on to the next
container with free cells: uniform,
then vest, then backpack.

What fits nowhere stays where it is,
shown apart in red. Nothing moves while
an arsenal is open - the arsenal gives
back what does not fit.

Switch it off to leave everything
where the engine put it.

How far from a player piles on the
ground and crates show in the loot
column on their own, in metres - and
how far away anything can still be
changed while the inventory is open.

Only what the player sees from where
they stand counts: nothing through
walls or from another floor.

Vehicles and bodies show when they
are opened, as before.

What can be used while it lies in the
backpack: magazines to reload from,
grenades to throw, bandages, food and
drink, kits and radios.

Everything: as in the game.
Only whitelisted: only items marked "Can
be used from" the backpack in the setup
wizard (Items step, rule use=backpack).
Nothing: nothing in the backpack can be
used, marked or not.
Strict (hidden): like Only whitelisted,
and the blocked items are kept out of
the backpack altogether, in a hidden
holder on the unit, so other mods cannot
use them. They still show in the
inventory (with a crossed eye), move,
drop and weigh as before.

A blocked item wears a padlock.

These limits are about using items in
the field. In the inventory window you
handle your gear freely: a magazine can
always be dragged onto a weapon or its
magazine slot, or loaded with "Load
into", from any container.

Enforced: the inventory window, the
hotbar, the window's menus, the reload
key, a reload from the action menu or a
gamepad (the magazine is taken back and
the fullest allowed one is loaded) and
the throw key, when only blocked
grenades are left.

Not enforced by Only whitelisted and
Nothing - a mod cannot change them: ACE
medical, rations and other mods that
read the unit's items themselves, ACE
Advanced Throwing picking what to throw,
a grenade of a type that also lies
elsewhere, scripts.

Strict keeps these items physically out
of the backpack in a hidden holder so
other mods cannot use them. This can
break mods or scripts that expect them
in the backpack (loadouts saved outside
an arsenal lack them, radios and kits
in it are unknown to their mods), and
may misbehave on respawn or with Zeus.
Use only if you need it.
